ANCHOR STORIES — Evening edition, Monday 20 July 2026 (17:55 BST)

Top 5 stories a competent UK editor would lead with today:

1. Andy Burnham becomes UK Prime Minister — Starmer steps down, King Charles asks
   Burnham to form a government; first speech at No 10 pledges a "circuit-breaker for
   Britain". Seventh PM in a decade. (Al Jazeera, CNN, NBC News, Irish Times, NPR)

2. Cabinet reshuffle — Rachel Reeves out as Chancellor, David Lammy out as Deputy PM;
   Burnham begins appointing a new cabinet. (Irish Times, Al Jazeera, CNBC)

3. US-Iran war Day 142 — third US service member killed (Iraq), ninth consecutive
   night of US strikes; Iran suspends MoU commitments; oil spikes above $90 then eases.
   (Times of Israel, CNN, Al Jazeera, CNBC)

4. Oil / Strait of Hormuz — Brent breaks $90 overnight then falls to ~$88 as Iran
   signals openness to talks; Hormuz traffic collapsed; Houthis declare embargo on
   Saudi Arabia. (CNBC, Al Jazeera, IEA)

5. Ukraine — Russian strike on grain ship near Odesa kills 10; Ukraine launches 400+
   drones at Moscow, hitting an oil depot; Kharkiv postal depot hit. (Al Jazeera)

COVERAGE CHECK: all five confirmed in approved-source retrievals. Cross-cutting UK
angle: Trump hails Burnham's North Sea oil plan while calling Britain a "Poverty
Stricken Disaster" (CNBC). Fiscal backdrop: £110bn debt-interest bill, Reform UK
leading/level in polls (Al Jazeera, YouGov, Survation). No major story (head-of-state
visit, market intervention, resignation) missing from the list.
